folders.title: DP 1
folders.description:
All answers will be found in the article.
Each question has between 1 and 5 true answers; questions are independent from one another.
Of note: type 2 diabetes will be referred to as Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) or Diabetes Mellitus (DM2)

questions.question: What is/ are the health-related overall benefit(s) of a vegan diet?
choix: A) Its rapid growth is also attributed to ethical concerns.
B) It decreases cancer incidence.
C) Plant-Based Diets (PBDs) rank among prevention measures when it comes to Diabetes Mellitus (DM2).
D) No Evidence-Based Medicine (EBM) has proved this point yet.
E) The aim of this article is to describe the relationship between vegan diets and the risk for Type 2 Diabetes (T2D).

questions.question: What is/ are the goal(s) of this research?
choix: A) To carry out a prospective study.
B) To determine -if any- a causal relationship between vegan diets and the risk for type 2 diabetes (T2D)
C) To describe the effect of the relationship between vegan diets and the risk for T2D on glycaemic control
D) To describe the effect of the relationship between vegan diets and the risk for T2D on T2D-related complications
E) To perform a scoping review of all interventional and observational studies

questions.question: How long did the study last?
choix: A) Until May 23rd, 2020
B) Up to 4 weeks
D) 2 years
E) Not stated in the article

questions.question: What was/ were the inclusion criterion/ criteria?
choix: A) Be over 18 years of age
B) Have pre-diabetes of diabetes type 1
C) Be on an omnivorous diet
D) Have a T2D diagnosis for randomised controlled studies
E) Be a healthy individual for observational studies

questions.question: Choose the true statement(s).
choix: A) three studies evaluated the waist circumference outcome and all of them reported its significant reduction in the intervention group
B) In the intervention groups, the changes in Systolic Blood Pressure (SBP) significantly varied
C) All studies noticed reduction in total cholesterol
D) In intervention groups, the statistical significance in LDL cholesterol was reached in three studies and in control groups in two studies
E) In intervention groups, the statistical significance in LDL cholesterol was reached in three studies and in control groups in two studies

questions.question: What was/ were the Main Outcome Measures (MOMs)?
choix: A) Nerve function in the case of randomised controlled studies
B) Prevalence or incidence of T2D in case of observational studies
C) Glycaemic control
D) Fasting glucose and Haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels and risk factors for diabetes related complications
E) Body Mass Index (BMI)

questions.question: Information finding in the results:
choix: A) All the observational studies considered were of acceptable quality
B) There were more studies looking at the incidence rate of T2D than studies looking at its prevalence
C) India’s third National Family Health Survey found a lower prevalence of T2D among vegans compared to non-vegetarians
D) All of the randomised controlled studies had at least a moderate risk of bias
E) Three of the studies reporting reductions in HbA1c levels after vegan diets were not statistically significant

questions.question: Which option(s) from this list is/ are limitations of the study?
choix: A) A final sample of 15 articles (7 observational and 8 randomised controlled studies) were included for this review
B) Renal function was impaired in both sets of studies: a significant increase in albuminuria was observed in the intervention group, while in the control group values, dropped insignificantly

C) Evaluation of the impact of the vegan diet on pain in chronic diabetic neuropathy was reported, reaching the statistically significant mean in-between group difference in favor of the 20-week intervention diet
D) The included observational studies had their diet assessments self-reported and in cross-sectional studies, the dietary habits may not be maintained over time
E) Vegan groups had mostly no restrictions in portion sizes, energy or carbohydrate intakes, contrary to some control groups

questions.question: What specific nutrient deficiency/-ies are vegans at risk of - thus impacting T2D management?
choix: A) Vitamin B12
B) Calcium
C) Vitamin D
D) Iron & zinc
E) Omega-3

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/ are true regarding the discussion and conclusion?
choix: A) Seventh-Day Adventists showed a significantly lower prevalence of T2D among vegetarians and vegans compared to omnivores.
B) The generalizability of the findings across different populations and cultures is mentioned as a limitation.
C) Weight loss is not a major factor in glycemia management.
D) Randomised controlled studies performed in T2D patients have shown an anti-hyperglycaemic effect of the vegan diet, even in the long term.
E) Future clinical trials should investigate the impact of the quantity and quality of carbohydrates in the vegan diet on pre-diabetes and T2D patients.

questions.question: When it comes to the significance of renal function findings in the study, how does albuminuria relate to the intervention group’s diet?
choix: A) Albuminuria is an early marker of renal involvement in diabetes and other kidney diseases.
B) The 2018 Barnard et al. study highlighted an increase in albuminuria in the intervention group.
C) T2D patients on a vegan diet are at higher risks of clinical implications (Barnard et al.- 2018).
D) The impact of the vegan diet on pain in chronic diabetic neuropathy has been evaluated (Bunner et al.).
E) All studies except Lee et al. reported albuminuria changes both the intervention and the control diet.
